name: ccmax-monitor-release-bot-doorward
description: semantic-release for doorward-systems/ccmax-monitor: push tags/commits, publish GitHub Releases + assets, comment on released issues & PRs. Injected as GH_TOKEN via `vault run ccmax-release`.
notes: semantic-release for doorward-systems/ccmax-monitor: push tags/commits, publish GitHub Releases + binary assets, comment on issues & PRs. Injected as GH_TOKEN via `vault run ccmax-release`; scripts/release-load-gh-token-from-secrets-file.sh mirrors it to GITHUB_TOKEN, which successCmd hard-requires. Closes issue #32, which recorded the stopgap of borrowing the operator's ambient `gh auth token` (a gho_* OAuth token carrying gist+read:org+repo across ALL repos) — bound to one human's interactive login, unusable unattended, and far broader than a release needs. Scoped to this repo only. REPO PATH CORRECTED 2026-08-28: this spec said terrylica/ccmax-monitor, but the repository now lives under the doorward-systems org. A fine-grained PAT's repository selection is owner-bound and does NOT follow a transfer — so the minted token kept working for READS (the redirect resolves, and the REST repo endpoint even reported permissions.push=true, which describes the USER not the token) while git refused every write with 'remote: Write access to repository not granted'. That failure surfaced only mid-release, as an infinite hang, because the machine's credential helper fell into an interactive OAuth flow instead of reporting the 403. The v3.1.0 release shipped on the operator's ambient gh token — i.e. it fell back to exactly the stopgap this spec exists to retire. RESOURCE OWNER ADDED 2026-09-04: the 2026-08-28 correction changed `repositoryAccess.repos` to the doorward-systems path but left `owner` unset, and `owner` is what actually drives GitHub's 'Resource owner' selector — scripts/form.mjs setOwner() returns on the first line when it is absent, leaving the form on its default (the authenticated USER) with repository access at 'Public Repositories (read-only)'. Editing only the repos array therefore produced a token that LOOKS repo-scoped in the spec and is account-scoped in reality; measured 2026-09-04, the minted token (sha256 0bc5d79ed5c1) sees 251 public repos, ZERO private, and GET /repos/doorward-systems/ccmax-monitor returns 404. A fine-grained PAT's repository picker only ever offers repositories belonging to the selected resource owner, so `owner` is not decoration duplicating the repos prefix — without it the repos entry cannot be honoured at all. RENAMED 2026-09-04 from `ccmax-monitor-release-bot` to `ccmax-monitor-release-bot-doorward`: a fine-grained PAT's name is unique per OWNING USER (terrylica) regardless of which resource owner it targets, so re-minting under the old name required `--replace`, which REVOKES the incumbent before the replacement is proven — leaving no working token if the mint or the org-approval step failed. A distinct name lets the broken user-owned token (id 17661881, sha256 0bc5d79ed5c1) stay live until the replacement passes a real write-capability check, after which the operator revokes it by hand. The `-doorward` suffix also names the resource owner, which is the exact axis the two tokens differ on and the one that was invisible in the old name. Nothing reads the token's display name — only the vault path `ccmax-release:gh.token` — so the rename is inert outside GitHub's own settings UI. EXPIRATION CHANGED 2026-09-04 from `none` to `366`: once the resource owner is the doorward-systems ORG, GitHub does not offer 'No expiration' at all — the org caps token lifetime and the menu is 7/30/60/90/366 days plus 'Custom between 1 and 366 days', labelled 'Limit set by doorward-systems'. The option is REMOVED, not disabled, so a spec asking for 'none' cannot be honoured and previously would have been downgraded in silence to the 30-day default. Note the corollary about the token this one replaces: sha256 0bc5d79ed5c1 is unexpiring ONLY because it was minted against the USER terrylica, where no org policy applies — its 'never expires' was itself a symptom of the wrong resource owner, not a property worth preserving. CONSEQUENCE FOR OPERATIONS: this token now expires 2027-09-05 and the release pipeline will break on that date unless it is rotated (`node scripts/pat.mjs rotate specs/ccmax-monitor-release-bot.json --vault ccmax-release:gh.token`). 366 days is the maximum the org permits; it cannot be raised from the spec, only by changing the doorward-systems organisation policy. MINT FAILURE ROOT CAUSE, 2026-09-04: the `description` above was previously this entire notes block (4272 chars) and GitHub SILENTLY dropped every submission — the confirmation dialog's submit closed the overlay, the form re-rendered with its defaults, no token was created and no error text appeared anywhere on the page. The description textarea advertises no maxlength (maxLength === -1), so nothing client-side objects. Cutting the description to 191 chars made the very next attempt succeed with every other field byte-identical, which is the control. Long-form reasoning now lives in this `notes` field, which the engine never types into the UI.
